children: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for Nvidia
to recruit an outside chief executive following Jensen Huang’s reported removal, raising questions about the chipmaker’s compliance practices ahead of its quarterly earnings release.
According to the supplied report, Bessent told Fox News’s
Sunday Morning Futures
that allegations
of Nvidia’s
advanced artificial-intelligence chips to China warrant changes beyond replacing the CEO.

“This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company,” he said. “That, just what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup.”
For investors, the developments bring leadership succession, export-control exposure and the reliability of compliance oversight into focus. The report says Nvidia
appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, leaving her to present quarterly results on Tuesday.
Bessent questioned whether Nvidia

overlooked signs that intermediaries, including shell companies in Singapore, were routing restricted chips to Chinese buyers. He urged the board and its outside lawyers to address whether commercial incentives influenced the company’s conduct.

“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said. “And I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the the board and from the outside counsel.”

The supplied report links Huang’s departure to allegations of an affair with a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International whom U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China. Those allegations, along with claims involving chip shipments, remain allegations; they should not be treated as established findings.
Bessent said the company’s legal review should help clarify its compliance practices.
“They brought in outside counsel, and I think we are going to get an explanation on this culture of noncompliance at Nvidia,” he told Fox News.

The controversy also puts the administration’s enforcement of semiconductor export restrictions under scrutiny. Bessent reiterated that he had supported adding Megaspeed to a trade blacklist, while identifying the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, as responsible for taking that step.
“As I said, many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen,” Bessent said Sunday.

According to the report, a Lutnick spokesperson told NBC News that the Commerce secretary had agreed to testify before Congress. Representative Jim Himes, the senior Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, also questioned whether Commerce had impeded efforts to prevent Nvidia chips from reaching China.

Meanwhile, lawmakers are advancing bipartisan proposals to tighten restrictions on AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Potential changes to those rules, and how aggressively existing restrictions are enforced, could affect Nvidia’s
access to customers and its revenue outlook.
Bessent argued that stronger enforcement of existing rules would be sufficient.
“I don’t think we need the legislation,” he said. “We have all the rules we need. We just need them enforced.”

title: Bessent calls for Nvidia leadership overhaul as export scrutiny intensifies
